fields.name: The log abundance conjecture in characteristic zero (rational boundary, every dimension), with canonical nonvanishing
fields.statement: For a projective log canonical pair $(X,B)$ the abundance conjecture of the minimal model program asserts that if the log canonical divisor $K_X+B$ is nef then it is semiample: some positive multiple is generated by global sections, so numerical positivity defines a morphism. The companion nonvanishing conjecture asserts that a pseudo-effective canonical class on a smooth projective variety has a nonzero pluricanonical section. Abundance was known in dimension at most three (Miyaoka, Kawamata, Keel-Matsuki-McKernan) and in special cases beyond. Is every nef $\mathbb Q$-Cartier $K_X+B$ on a projective log canonical pair with effective rational boundary, over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, semiample?
fields.posedBy: Central conjecture of the minimal model program (Kawamata, Miyaoka, Reid and others); the manuscripts name no single poser and cite its threefold history
fields.ageNote: The manuscripts do not say who posed the conjecture or when. Its threefold cases were proved between 1988 and 1994 (Miyaoka, Kawamata, Keel-Matsuki-McKernan), and it has been a standing conjecture of the minimal model program since the 1980s.

Family 034 has fourteen manuscripts dated September 24 to October 5, 2026, which cite one another as inputs; this entry draws on the manuscript named as its source. The manuscript is credited to 'OpenAI' alone, names no human author and has no acknowledgements. The README's two exceptions to the fixed procedure (the zeta zero-free region work, whose Re(s) > 11/12 write-up was also human-edited, and the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties) do not concern this family, so the result is presented as found and written up by the model. The release does not say how problems were chosen or how much human review happened before publication.
fields.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Checked here: Theorem 1.1 and the introduction of 'Log abundance in characteristic zero' were read against the conjecture as stated there; the claim is unconditional and covers every dimension. The proof (a dimension induction using a signed-boundary criterion, Hodge-module lifting through infinitesimal neighbourhoods and Hashizume's reduction to smooth nonvanishing) was not refereed. No Lean formalization. A reader should know that the release is not consistent about whether projective abundance is unconditional: the October 5 companion on Kahler fourfolds proves projective log abundance in its appendices and calls it a conditional resolution, not an unconditional abundance theorem, assuming logarithmic Iitaka subadditivity, while this September 24 manuscript claims it outright. The family's effective Iitaka, index and Campana-Peternell results use this manuscript as an input. Listed as Contested because the release itself disagrees on whether the theorem is conditional; see the claim issue.
fields.resultNote: Theorem 1.1: for a normal projective lc pair $(X,B)$ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, with $B$ effective rational and $K_X+B$ $\mathbb Q$-Cartier and nef, some positive Cartier multiple of $K_X+B$ is globally generated. The induction also gives good minimal models for lc pairs with pseudo-effective real adjoint and, over $\mathbb C$, canonical nonvanishing for smooth projective varieties in every dimension; consequences include rational slc abundance (Fujino-Gongyo) and finite generation of lc rings. Not shown: semiampleness with real boundaries, positive characteristic, or any bound on the multiple. The family's compact Kahler log abundance theorem assumes logarithmic Iitaka subadditivity (claimed in family 033) and is not part of this entry.

fields.significanceNote: Abundance with nonvanishing is the central open conjecture of the minimal model program, open from dimension four on for decades. Placed above the 67 percent critical-line result (68) and the Jacobian Conjecture (65), and below the unforced 3D Euler blowup entry (80) and the Navier-Stokes entry (87), as a problem central to one large field rather than to all of mathematics.
fields.claimIssueNote: The release contradicts itself on this claim. The 24 September manuscript's abstract states that the rational-boundary log abundance conjecture is proved in every dimension. An appendix of the release's own 5 October manuscript on compact Kahler fourfolds calls the same theorem "a positive conditional resolution of the log abundance conjecture. It is not an unconditional abundance theorem", resting on a logarithmic Iitaka subadditivity assumption that it says follows from a lemma elsewhere in the release. Until OpenAI clarifies which reading is meant, or a specialist checks the chain, the entry is Contested.

fields.name: The effective Iitaka fibration conjecture
fields.statement: For a smooth projective variety $X$ with Kodaira dimension $\kappa(X)\ge0$, the pluricanonical systems $|mK_X|$ define the Iitaka fibration for all sufficiently large divisible $m$. For varieties of general type, Hacon-McKernan, Takayama and Tsuji found one $m$ depending only on $\dim X$; Birkar and Zhang proved an effective bound that also depends on invariants of the general fibre. Is there, for each $d$, an integer $m(d)$ such that $|m(d)K_X|$ defines the Iitaka fibration of every smooth projective $d$-fold with $\kappa(X)\ge0$?

fields.ageNote: The question predates the 2016 statement: Fujino-Mori (2000) and Viehweg-Zhang (2009) proved cases, as the manuscript recounts.

fields.name: The index conjecture for semi-log-canonical log Calabi-Yau pairs with finite rational coefficient sets
fields.statement: A projective log Calabi-Yau pair $(X,B)$ has $K_X+B\sim_{\mathbb Q}0$, so some positive multiple $m(K_X+B)$ is Cartier and linearly trivial; the least such $m$ is the index. Gongyo showed such $m$ exists for slc pairs, but it may depend on the pair. The index conjecture asks for uniformity. In its finite-rational-coefficient slc form, fix $d$ and a finite set $\Phi\subset[0,1]\cap\mathbb Q$: is there an integer $a(d,\Phi)$ such that $a(d,\Phi)(K_X+B)$ is Cartier and trivial for every connected projective slc log Calabi-Yau pair of dimension $d$ with coefficients in $\Phi$?

fields.ageNote: The manuscript cites Jiang-Liu (arXiv 2020, published 2021) as one place the conjecture is stated, not as its origin. The normal-pair index conjecture is older; Xu (2019) organized reductions between its forms. Jiang-Liu proved the slc case in dimension at most three.

fields.name: The effective log Iitaka conjecture for log canonical pairs with finite rational coefficient sets
fields.statement: Chen, Han and Liu conjectured a logarithmic version of effective Iitaka fibrations: for fixed dimension $d$ and a DCC set $\Phi\subset[0,1]$, one integer $m$ should make the rounded system $|\lfloor m(K_X+B)\rfloor|$ nonempty with section ratios generating the Iitaka field, for every projective lc pair $(X,B)$ of dimension $d$ with coefficients in $\Phi$ and nonnegative Kodaira dimension. They proved it in dimension at most three. Does it hold in every dimension when $\Phi$ is a finite set of rationals?

fields.name: Birkar's Stein-degree conjecture for log Calabi-Yau pairs: the contraction-to-a-point case for ordinary pairs
fields.statement: For a proper integral variety $S$ over a field $k$ the Stein degree is $\dim_k H^0(S,\mathcal O_S)$. Birkar conjectured that boundary components of log Calabi-Yau fibrations with coefficient bounded below have uniformly bounded Stein degree; Birkar and Qu proved normalized bounds over algebraically closed fields of characteristic zero. For a contraction to a point over any field $k$ of characteristic zero: given $d$ and $t>0$, is there $N(d,t)$ such that for every projective lc pair $(X,B)$ of dimension $d$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$ and $K_X+B\sim_{\mathbb Q}0$, every prime component of $B$ with coefficient at least $t$ has Stein degree at most $N(d,t)$?

fields.name: The Campana-Peternell conjecture on Kodaira dimension
fields.statement: Campana and Peternell, studying positivity of the cotangent bundle, conjectured that if $NK_X=A+B$ on a smooth projective variety $X$, with $N>0$, $A$ effective and $B$ pseudo-effective, then $\kappa(X)\ge\kappa(A)$. The case $A=0$ is canonical nonvanishing. Schnell reduced the conjecture, given nonvanishing, to fibrations whose fibres have Kodaira dimension zero. Is it true that for every smooth connected projective complex variety $X$, effective Cartier divisor $D$ and integer $m_0>0$ with $m_0K_X-D$ pseudo-effective, $\kappa(X)\ge\kappa(D)$?
